texts.987ba05aae67: The data supplied will be used only for the approved medical research project MR785 - PD MED Trial- A randomised assessment of the cost of different classes of drugs for Parkinson's
texts.f48f93d81e0b: Previous clinical trials comparing different drug therapies for Parkinson’s disease (PD) have generally been too small for reliable conclusions, have used inappropriate surrogate endpoints and follow-up has been too short to evaluate long-term benefits and toxicity. This large pragmatic, “real-life” randomised trial addresses four fundamental, unanswered questions about PD treatment. Does initial treatment with levodopa-sparing therapy (either a dopamine agonist (DA) or a monoamine oxidase B Inhibitor (MAOBI)) delay the progress of disability compared to levodopa (LD) alone. If so which class of LD-sparing treatment is preferable (DA or MAOBI). For patients with motor fluctuations uncontrolled by LD alone, should DAs or dopamine degradation inhibitors (DDIs) be added to LD and which class of DDI (MAOBI or catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibitor (COMTI)) is the most clinically and cost-effective. PDMED will evaluate long-term safety and efficacy based principally on patients’ evaluation of their functioning and overall health-related qulaity of life, with a sample size large enough to give clear and reliable results
